verses.1:1: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have obtained a faith equal with ours in the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.
verses.1:2: May grace and peace be brought to fullness for you in the knowledge of God and of Christ Jesus our Lord,
verses.1:3: as all things of His divine power that are for life and godliness have been granted to us through the knowledge of Him who called us by His own glory and virtue,
verses.1:4: through whom He has granted us the greatest and precious promises, so that through these you may become sharers of the divine nature, fleeing the corruption of that lust which is in the world.
verses.1:5: Now you, applying all diligence, supply in your faith virtue, and in virtue knowledge,
verses.1:6: and in knowledge self-restraint, and in self-restraint patience, and in patience godliness,
verses.1:7: and in godliness affection for the brotherhood, and in affection for the brotherhood love.
verses.1:8: For if these things are present with you and abound, they will make you neither idle nor without fruit in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:9: For the one to whom these things are not at hand is blind and groping by hand, falling into forgetfulness of the cleansing of his former sins.
verses.1:10: Therefore, brothers, be all the more diligent to make your calling and election sure through good works; for in doing these things, you will never sin.
verses.1:11: For in this way an entrance will be abundantly supplied to you into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.
verses.1:12: For this reason I will begin always to remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the present truth.
verses.1:13: And I consider it right, as long as I am in this tent, to rouse you by way of reminder,
verses.1:14: being certain that the laying aside of my tent is swift, just as our Lord Jesus Christ also made clear to me.
verses.1:15: And I will make every effort so that after my departure you may also frequently be able to call these things to remembrance.
verses.1:16: For we made known to you the power and presence of our Lord Jesus Christ not by following cleverly crafted fables, but having become observers of His majesty.
verses.1:17: For He received honor and glory from God the Father when a voice of this kind came down to Him from the magnificent Glory: "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to Him."
verses.1:18: And we ourselves heard this voice brought from heaven when we were with Him on the holy mountain.
verses.1:19: And we have a firmer prophetic word, to which you do well to pay attention, as to a lamp shining in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts,
verses.1:20: understanding this first: that no prophecy of Scripture comes about by one's own interpretation.
verses.1:21: For prophecy was never brought by human will, but inspired by the Holy Spirit, holy men of God spoke.
verses.2:1: Yet there were also false prophets among the people, just as there will also be lying teachers among you, who will introduce sects of destruction; and they deny the Lord who bought them, bringing swift destruction upon themselves.
verses.2:2: And many will follow their debaucheries, through whom the way of truth will be blasphemed;
verses.2:3: and in greed they will traffic in you with fabricated words; for them judgment from long ago is not idle, and their destruction does not slumber.
verses.2:4: For if God did not spare the angels when they sinned, but handed them over, dragged down with ropes of the underworld into Tartarus to be tormented, to be reserved for judgment;
verses.2:5: and did not spare the original world, but guarded Noah, the eighth person, a herald of righteousness, bringing a flood upon the world of the ungodly;
verses.2:6: and reducing the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah to ashes, condemned them to overthrow, setting them as an example of those who are about to act impiously;
verses.2:7: and rescued righteous Lot, oppressed by the outrage and debauched conduct of abominable men
verses.2:8: (for in sight and hearing he was righteous, dwelling among those who from day to day tormented his righteous soul with unjust deeds),
verses.2:9: then the Lord knows how to rescue the godly from trial, yet to reserve the unjust for the day of judgment to be tormented,
verses.2:10: and especially those who walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness and despise dominion. Bold, pleasing themselves, they do not fear to introduce sects, blaspheming,
verses.2:11: whereas angels, though they are greater in strength and power, do not bring a reviling judgment against themselves.
verses.2:12: But these, like irrational beasts, by nature for capture and for ruin, blaspheming in the things they do not know, will perish in their own corruption,
verses.2:13: receiving the wages of unrighteousness, counting daytime luxuries as pleasure; defilements and blemishes, overflowing with luxuries, reveling with you in their banquets,
verses.2:14: having eyes full of adultery and of unceasing sin. Enticing unstable souls, having a heart trained in greed, children of a curse,
verses.2:15: abandoning the straight way, they have gone astray, having followed the way of Balaam from Bosor, who loved the wages of iniquity;
verses.2:16: yet he received a rebuke for his own madness: a mute beast of burden, speaking with a man's voice, restrained the folly of the prophet.
verses.2:17: These are springs without water and mists driven by whirlwinds, for whom the gloom of darkness is reserved.
verses.2:18: For speaking proud words of emptiness, they entice through desires of fleshly debauchery those who are barely escaping those who live in error,
verses.2:19: promising them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption; for by whomever someone is overcome, of him he is also a slave.
verses.2:20: For if, fleeing the defilements of the world in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are entangled in these again and overcome, their latter state has become worse for them than the former.
verses.2:21: For it would have been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness than, after acknowledging it, to turn back from that holy commandment which was handed down to them.
verses.2:22: For that saying of the true proverb has happened to them: "A dog returned to its own vomit," and, "A washed sow in a wallow of mud."
verses.3:1: Look, beloved, I am writing this second letter to you, in which I stir up your sincere mind by way of reminder,
verses.3:2: so that you may be mindful of those words which I spoke beforehand from the holy prophets, and of your apostles' precepts of the Lord and Savior.
verses.3:3: Knowing this first: that in the last days mockers will come in deception, walking according to their own lusts
verses.3:4: and saying, "Where is the promise, or His coming? For since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue in this way from the beginning of creation."
verses.3:5: For this willfully escapes their notice: that the heavens existed before, and the earth standing together out of water and through water by the word of God,
verses.3:6: through which the world of that time, flooded with water, perished.
verses.3:7: But the heavens that now exist, and the earth, have been stored up by the same word, reserved for fire for the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.
verses.3:8: Yet let this one thing not escape your notice, beloved, that with the Lord one day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
verses.3:9: The Lord does not delay His promise, as some suppose, but acts patiently for your sake, not wishing any to perish, but all to return to repentance.
verses.3:10: Yet the day of the Lord will come like a thief, in which the heavens will pass away with great force, and the elements will be dissolved by heat, and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.
verses.3:11: Since, therefore, all these things are to be dissolved, what sort of people ought you to be in holy ways of life and acts of godliness,
verses.3:12: awaiting and hastening toward the coming of the day of the Lord, through which the heavens, burning, will be dissolved, and the elements will melt in the blaze of fire?
verses.3:13: Yet we await new heavens and a new earth according to His promises, in which righteousness dwells.
verses.3:14: For this reason, beloved, awaiting these things, be diligent to be found by Him spotless and unblemished in peace,
verses.3:15: and consider the forbearance of our Lord to be salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom given to him,
verses.3:16: as also in all his letters, speaking in them about these matters, in which there are certain things difficult to understand, which the unlearned and unstable distort, as they also do the rest of the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
verses.3:17: You, therefore, brothers, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard so that, led away by the error of the foolish, you do not fall from your own steadfastness;
verses.3:18: but grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To Him be glory both now and to the day of eternity. Amen.

notes.1:4: The Vulgate reads "through whom" (per quem, masculine singular, referring back to the one who called us in 1:3), whereas the Greek reads "through which" (plural, referring to glory and virtue).
notes.1:9: Latin "groping by hand" (manu tentans) is a Vulgate-distinct rendering where the Greek means "nearsighted" or "closing the eyes."
notes.1:10: The Vulgate includes "through good works" (per bona opera), reflecting a variant Greek manuscript tradition absent from modern critical Greek editions.
notes.1:17: The Vulgate adds "listen to Him" (ipsum audite) at the end of the Transfiguration voice (compare Matt 17:5), a clause absent from modern critical Greek editions of 2 Peter.
notes.1:21: The Vulgate reads "inspired by the Holy Spirit" (Spiritu Sancto inspirati) and "holy men of God" (sancti Dei homines), whereas critical Greek editions read "carried along by the Holy Spirit" and "men from God."
notes.2:4: The Vulgate reads "with ropes of the underworld" (rudentibus inferni) and adds "to be tormented" (cruciandos), whereas modern critical Greek editions read "chains" or "pits of gloom" without the added phrase.
notes.2:8: Unlike the Greek, in which Lot torments his own righteous soul, the Vulgate uses a plural verb (cruciabant) so that the wicked inhabitants of Sodom are the ones who tormented Lot's righteous soul from day to day.
notes.2:10: The Vulgate reads "they do not fear to introduce sects" (sectas non metuunt introducere), whereas the Greek speaks of not trembling to blaspheme "glorious ones" (angelic majesties).
notes.2:11: The Vulgate uses the reflexive "against themselves" (adversum se) and omits "before the Lord," whereas Greek manuscripts read "against them before the Lord."
notes.2:15: The Vulgate preserves "from Bosor" (ex Bosor, matching the Greek New Testament form Bosor), whereas the Old Testament Hebrew names Balaam's father "Beor" (Num 22:5).
notes.3:2: The Vulgate uniquely reads a first-person active verb, "which I spoke beforehand" (quae praedixi), and plural "precepts" (praeceptorum), whereas the Greek has a passive participle ("spoken beforehand by the holy prophets") and singular "commandment."
notes.3:4: The Vulgate reads "the promise, or His coming" (promissio, aut adventus ejus), joining the two nouns with "or" where the Greek reads "the promise of His coming."
notes.3:10: The Vulgate reads "will be burned up" (exurentur), matching the majority Greek tradition rather than the reading "will be found" (or "exposed") in modern critical Greek editions.
notes.3:17: The Vulgate reads "of the foolish" (insipientium), whereas the Greek reads "of the lawless."
